item.title: Sri Lanka make 430 to beat England despite Harry Brook's 202
item.description:
CRICKET-ENG-SRI-ODI

Sri Lanka scripted a remarkable victory over England in the third match of the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series 2026 on Thursday, chasing down a massive target of 430 after Harry Brook’s record-breaking double century powered England to 429/4 in Rawalpindi.

With this remarkable victory, Sri Lanka scripted history by completing the second-highest successful run chase in ODI cricket, gunning down England’s massive target of 430 in a sensational contest.

England's magnificent Brook hits fastest ODI double century

The highest successful chase in the format remains South Africa’s historic pursuit of 435 against Australia in Johannesburg in 2006, when they reached 438/9 to secure a thrilling one-wicket victory.

In a high-scoring thriller, Sri Lanka produced a sensational batting display to overcome the massive target and register a memorable win, despite Brook’s historic knock that saw him become the first English batter to score a double century in men’s ODI cricket.

Brook smashed 202 off just 116 deliveries, registering the fastest double century in ODI history. His innings was studded with 21 fours and 10 sixes. Joe Root provided valuable support with 69 off 66 balls, while Will Jacks struck an unbeaten 66 off just 30 deliveries to propel England to their imposing total.

Sri Lanka’s chase got off to a shaky start as they lost two early wickets. However, Avishka Fernando and Pavan Rathnayake staged a remarkable recovery with a crucial partnership that brought the hosts back into the contest.

Fernando narrowly missed out on a century, scoring 97 off 83 balls, while Rathnayake produced a magnificent 130 off 106 deliveries to keep Sri Lanka firmly in the hunt.

Dasun Shanaka then delivered a breathtaking counterattack, smashing 97 off just 50 balls, including eight sixes, to turn the momentum in Sri Lanka’s favour.

Like Fernando, Shanaka fell just three runs short of a century, but his explosive innings brought the target within reach and set the stage for a thrilling finish.

Janith Liyanage played a crucial role in the closing stages, contributing an unbeaten half-century as Sri Lanka maintained their charge to complete the extraordinary run chase.

item.title: Earthquake of magnitude 7 strikes China's Tibet
item.description:
An earthquake of magnitude 7 struck China's southwestern region of Tibet at around 10:33 p.m. (1433 GMT) on Thursday, the China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC) said.

It was not immediately known if there were any casualties or damage.

The epicentre was in a high-altitude county in Nagqu, northern Tibet, at a depth of 10 km (6.21 miles), and the average elevation within 5 km of the epicentre is about 4,864 metres, CENC data showed.

The quake, the strongest to hit China since January 2024, was clearly felt in the local area, CENC said. The epicentre was around 400 km from the Tibetan capital of Lhasa.

In 2010, a magnitude 7.1 tremor struck Yushu, around 280 km away in neighbouring Qinghai province, killing at least 2,698 people and leaving nearly 300 people missing.

item.title: Saudi airport attacks disrupt 135 flights from Bangladesh, affect 20,672 passengers
item.description:
A total of 135 flights operating between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia, both direct and via transit routes, have had to be suspended or cancelled due to restrictions on flight operations at Saudi airports.

As a result, 20,672 passengers on these flights have been affected. Of the cancelled or suspended flights, 62 were direct flights and 73 were transit flights.

The Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) disclosed this information in a press release on Thursday afternoon.

According to CAAB, the direct flights included 23 operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, 10 by US-Bangla Airlines, 19 by Saudia and 10 by Riyadh Air.

Among the transit flights, 28 were operated by IndiGo, 14 by Emirates, nine by Qatar Airways, eight by flydubai, seven by SalamAir, six by Air India and one by EgyptAir.

Flights at various airports across Saudi Arabia were suspended following attacks by Yemen's armed Houthi group on airports in different parts of the country, including the capital Riyadh.

Even after the airports resumed operations, many airlines have continued to suspend their flights there, depending on the prevailing situation.

Meanwhile, a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight carrying 379 passengers departed Dhaka for Dammam airport in Saudi Arabia on Thursday morning.

However, Dammam airport came under another attack on Wednesday night, raising uncertainty over whether flights to Dammam will continue. Biman Bangladesh Airlines authorities would hold a meeting tonight, Thursday to decide on the matter.

Saudi Arabia airport attack: Identity of 2 injured Bangladeshis confirmed
item.description:
IRAN-CRISIS-SAUDI-AIRPORT

An attack took place at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, in eastern Saudi Arabia, on Wednesday, leaving at least two people dead and eight others injured, including two Bangladeshis.

The Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment confirmed the identity of the Bangladeshis in a press release on Thursday.

The injured expatriate Bangladeshis are Sajal Chandra Das, son of Anukul Chandra Das of Ramchandrapur Union under Bangra Bazar police station in Cumilla, and Mohammad Abdur Rahim, son of Sirajul Haque of Dinmonirhat in Noakhali Sadar upazila.

In a press release issued on Thursday, the Ministry said that two Bangladeshis were injured in an attack targeting King Fahd International Airport in Dammam at around 9:00 pm on 21 October, Wednesday. They are currently receiving treatment at Saudi German Hospital in Dammam. Representatives of the Bangladesh Embassy visited the injured at the hospital and enquired about their treatment.

The Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare said the two injured Bangladeshis had lost consciousness due to heat and smoke. They have no signs of serious physical injuries. They are now in good health and have spoken with embassy representatives. They may be discharged from the hospital on Friday.

A report published by Qatar-based Al Jazeera on Wednesday said that airports across Saudi Arabia, including those in the capital Riyadh, have been targeted in a series of attacks in recent times. The incident at King Fahd International Airport is the latest in this series of attacks.

In an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on 10 October, 12 people were killed and more than 300 injured. Another attack was carried out on a Saudi airport the following day, 11 October. According to information provided by Saudi authorities, one person was killed and 11 others injured in that attack.

The internationally recognised government of Yemen is engaged in intense fighting against the Iran-backed armed group Houthis over control of large parts of the country. The Saudi-led multinational coalition is fighting against the Houthis.

item.title: Seven Qawmi-based parties mull alliance under Hefazat’s guidance
item.description:
Seven Islamic political parties belonging to the Qawmi madrasa tradition have discussed whether they can contest local government elections together as an alliance. However, no decision has been made yet. The issue will be discussed further at the next meeting on 5 December, with informal discussions to continue in the meantime.

The discussion took place at a meeting of the liaison committee of the seven parties at Al-Jamiatul Islamia Makhzanul Ulum (Dhaka) madrasa in Khilgaon, the capital, on Thursday.

The alliance-building process involves Islami Andolan Bangladesh, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh, Khelafat Majlis, Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis, Bangladesh Khelafat Andolon, Islami Oikya Jote and Bangladesh Nezam-e-Islam Party.

The meeting was chaired by Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh Secretary General Maulana Sajidur Rahman. It began at 10:30am and continued until 1pm, with members of the seven parties’ liaison committees in attendance. Hefazat organising secretary Mufti Bashir Ullah, its Narayanganj district president Maulana Abdul Awal and Mufti Ayub Babunagari, son of the organisation’s ameer, also attended.

According to sources at the meeting, discussions covered the structure of the seven-party alliance, joint activities under a common banner, relations with other political alliances and future plans. The next meeting, scheduled for 5 December, will further discuss the alliance’s principles and working procedures.

Leaders who attended the meeting said Jamaat-e-Islami wants to contest local government elections independently. Against this backdrop, discussions have begun on how the parties in the 11-party electoral alliance led by Jamaat will participate in local elections. As the seven-party unity initiative among Qawmi-based parties progresses, the meeting also discussed whether parties currently in that alliance could contest elections under the new banner.

Bangladesh Nezam-e-Islam Party Secretary General Musa Bin Izhar told Prothom Alo that the meeting discussed whether the seven parties could contest local government elections together. He said they viewed the discussion positively and that his party would participate if the seven parties contested the local elections as an alliance.

Islami Andolan Bangladesh Secretary General Gazi Ataur Rahman also said preliminary discussions had taken place on whether the seven parties could contest local government elections together.

He told Prothom Alo that the issue would be discussed further at the 5 December meeting, with informal discussions possible in the meantime.

Seven parties to operate under ‘Like-minded Islamic Parties’ banner

Leaders who attended the meeting said the seven Islamic parties would work together under the banner of Samomona Islami Dol (Like-minded Islamic Parties), while retaining their separate identities.

Hefazat organising secretary Mufti Bashir Ullah told Prothom Alo that the parties had decided to remain united under the banner. They had also discussed the basis for the alliance, but its working procedures had not yet been finalised. Another meeting had therefore been scheduled for 5 December, he said.

Two parties object to alliance conditions

Leaders who attended the meeting said that although a policy-level decision had been taken to conduct joint activities under the common banner of like-minded Islamic Parties, no consensus had been reached on whether parties belonging to other political alliances would have to leave those alliances.

According to sources at the meeting, Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis and Bangladesh Nezam-e-Islam Party objected to imposing such a condition on parties that belong to other political alliances. They argued that the matter required further discussion.

Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis Joint Secretary General Ataullah Amin told Prothom Alo that the meeting had discussed a proposal barring any party in the seven-party alliance from belonging to another alliance. Hefazat-e-Islam had asked parties that were members of other alliances to leave them, he said. No final decision had been reached on the matter.

Musa Bin Izhar, secretary general of Bangladesh Nezam-e-Islam Party, also said Hefazat leaders had asked Qawmi-based parties to withdraw from the 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami.

He told Prothom Alo that his party would remain under the like-minded Islamic Parties banner. However, it would also continue participating in the 11-party alliance’s movement to implement the July Charter and the outcome of the referendum.

Hefazat organising secretary Mufti Bashir Ullah told Prothom Alo that a decision had been taken that the seven parties could not belong to any other alliance. However, some parties had said they would discuss the matter within their respective party forums before communicating their positions, he said.

According to sources at the meeting, the parties’ relations with Jamaat-e-Islami and the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) were also discussed. During the discussion, the secretary general of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh said his party would leave the BNP-led alliance if the seven-party alliance was formed.

Leaders who attended the meeting also said Hefazat Secretary General Maulana Sajidur Rahman emphasised the importance of reaching consensus through discussions within the parties’ liaison committees before making political decisions. He also said further discussions could be held on whether the conditions regarding membership in other political alliances could be relaxed.

Other issues discussed

According to sources at the meeting, a leader of Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis raised the issue of negative remarks about his party’s ameer, Maulana Mamunul Haque, as well as social media campaigns and the publication of a book concerning him. Hefazat Secretary General Sajidur Rahman condemned such incidents and activities, the sources said.

The meeting also discussed objectionable social media posts by Hefazat leader Harun Azizi about leaders of Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis. Mufti Ayub Babunagari, son of the Hefazat ameer, was assigned to investigate the matter.

Participants also discussed and criticised various issues relating to the implementation of the July National Charter and remarks made by several political leaders during the recent Durga Puja celebrations.

item.title: 20 more Bangladeshis on Saudi convict list, sentences undisclosed
item.description:
The word ‘convicted’ is written next to the names of 22 Bangladeshi citizens imprisoned in Saudi Arabia.

However, the list sent by the Saudi government does not specify their punishment, whether they have been sentenced to prison, or given the death penalty. The Bangladesh Consulate in Jeddah is also unaware.

Among these 22 individuals were Nazrul Islam and Sweety Akhtar, whose death penalty execution news has sparked outrage among the people of Bangladesh. The fate of the remaining 20 individuals is now uncertain.

The Bangladesh Consulate in Jeddah has sent a letter to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Saudi Arabia to find out what punishment has been given to them.

The Bangladesh Consulate in Jeddah sent the letter to the Jeddah branch of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Saudi Arabia on 19 October.

When asked, Mohammad Shakawat Hossain, the Consul General of Bangladesh in Jeddah, told Prothom Alo on Thursday that clear information has been sought from the Saudi authorities to ensure consular services for convicted citizens of Bangladesh.

Questions over empty punishment column

On 30 September, the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs sent a list of 2,461 Bangladeshi prisoners. Some of these prisoners under the jurisdiction of the Bangladesh Consulate in Jeddah have been tried and sentenced, while others’ cases are ongoing. Upon reviewing the list, the Consulate noticed that although several individuals have ‘convicted’ written in the ‘status’ column, their ‘verdict summary’ column is empty. Neither the type nor the duration of the punishment is mentioned.

The Consulate requested the Makkah region branch (Jeddah) of the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs on 19 October to coordinate with the relevant authorities and send the verdict summaries promptly. The letter stated that this information is necessary for carrying out consular duties. The enclosed 9-page list includes descriptions of the prisoners. However, the letter does not specify how many columns are empty. Counting from the attached list, 22 individuals are found.

Nature of cases against the 22 individuals

Sources at the Bangladesh Consulate in Jeddah have reported, according to the list provided by Saudi Arabia, that among the 22 individuals, 8 have been prosecuted for murder, 5 for drug trafficking, and 5 for ‘personal rights’ cases. Two cases pertain to violations of state law, one to cybercrime, and one to adultery.

Six are in Jeddah’s Dhahban Prison, six in Shumaisi, four in Jeddah General Prison, and the remaining six in women’s prisons in Najran, Khamis, Al-Baha, Hada, and Jeddah.

Notably, all five individuals involved in ‘personal rights’ cases are in Shumaisi prison. Typically, such cases involve personal claims or compensation, but without case documents, the exact allegations are uncertain.

However, the type of case does not imply the punishment. Under Saudi law, a murder case may result in qisas (death penalty), or it could be resolved with blood money or imprisonment. Thus, it cannot be assumed whether anyone in the list has received the death penalty or not.

The risk of not knowing the verdict

The consequences of not knowing the verdict after a serious criminal conviction in Saudi Arabia are exemplified by the recent execution of Nazrul Islam and Sweety Akhtar. Without a verdict summary, the Consulate doesn’t know which paths are open for individuals. Whether an appeal is possible, how a lawyer can be appointed, or if resolving through blood money or pardon is feasible—all depend on the verdict. Families back home are also living in the same uncertainty. For this reason, the Bangladesh Consulate in Jeddah has taken special initiatives following the execution news of Nazrul and Sweety.

In the letter sent by the Jeddah Consulate to the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs, it is stated that the request to learn details of the sentences of the convicted Bangladeshis aims to update their database and provide the best consular services to the citizens. Hence, without filling the gaps in the list, the Consulate’s records also remain incomplete. It remains to be seen how quickly the Saudi authorities provide the verdict information and what penalties are revealed for each individual.

Request for pardon and repatriation

On 19 October, the Jeddah Consulate made a special request in another letter by categorizing the 2,461 prisoners into five groups. It requested the rapid release and return of prisoners whose sentences have been completed, inclusion of well-behaved prisoners in the royal pardon list, waiving remaining punishment for first-time detainees and those charged with petty crimes, and expedite the resolution of pending cases.

The Consulate has also written to the Saudi Ministry about two other Bangladeshis. Their families have reported that the security forces have arrested them, but they do not know why they were arrested or from where they were taken.

The response from the Saudi authorities regarding these letters from the Consulate has not yet been received.

item.title: PHP flaws prompt millions of hacking attempts amid rush to patch vulnerabilities
item.description:
CYBERSECURITY-PHP/

Global firms and governments rushed on Thursday to patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet, as a cloud firm reported millions of hacking attempts after vulnerabilities were disclosed.

The push came after governments in Europe and elsewhere took websites offline as a precaution on Wednesday while website operators scrambled to secure systems running the software.

The emergency shutdowns of banking, airline, rail, tax and government services from Tokyo to Helsinki mark one of the most dramatic tests of the decades-old programming tools that keep the web running, exposing how deeply governments and companies depend on code that few people understand.

"I've not seen anything like this in a long, long time," Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said at an event in Germany on Thursday, saying the incident showed the importance of building software that can be maintained securely as systems grow more complex.

"It was a long day and a long night, I know, for all the IT and security folks."

PHP key to internet's foundations like html, python

The developers of PHP - a key computing language like HTML and Python - released fixes on Wednesday for vulnerabilities that had lurked in the software for years until they were uncovered using AI, urging users to "update immediately".

Madeline Lawrence, co-founder of Belgian cybersecurity firm Aikido Security, said that details of the flaws had become public before fixes were ready, with attacks reported since.

"Companies are racing to update against attackers who can use AI to exploit them. That's the whole race," she said.

As companies and governments deployed patches and suspended websites as a precaution, hacking attempts surged into the millions, according to cloud services firm Cloudflare.

"In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it," Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince said in a post on X late on Wednesday.

"That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now."

Impact from Japan to Finland

Japanese companies including brokerage Nomura, lender Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, airline ANA and East Japan Railway said on Thursday they were temporarily suspending some internet services as part of emergency measures.

Brewer Asahi Group Holdings temporarily suspended certain websites and systems and was conducting a security impact assessment. Insurer Tokio Marine Holdings said it had suspended its group website.

Japan's Ministry of Finance and Meteorological Agency partially suspended online services to implement safety measures, while Japan's National Tax Agency temporarily took down its service.

The precautionary shutdowns show Japan's growing concerns over cybersecurity, as the country recorded more cyber incidents in the first nine months of the year than in all of last year, according to data from TrendAI.

French telecoms group Orange said it had temporarily suspended access to certain PHP-based websites and applications across several subsidiaries as a precaution.

Tencent Cloud, one of China's largest cloud-computing providers, urged customers to install updated PHP versions but stopped short of calling for widespread website shutdowns.

Finland's state IT services provider Valtori said it had continued installing PHP security patches overnight and was gradually lifting precautionary service blocks after shutting down government public web services a day earlier.

"Restoring services can take days or even weeks, as in addition to updates, the systems need to be carefully tested," Valtori Director General Hannu Naumanen said in a statement.

Valtori said the outages were not caused by exploitation of the vulnerabilities or by a cyber breach, and that it was not aware of any active exploitation of the flaws.

Some fixes may take weeks to implement

Several Asian governments ordered cybersecurity inspections related to the PHP vulnerabilities on Thursday.

China's industry ministry urged organizations and users to inspect systems and upgrade to the latest secure version of PHP. It also recommended strengthening cybersecurity monitoring and changing accounts, passwords and keys where necessary.

South Korea raised its private-sector cybersecurity alert level and activated emergency response measures, citing concerns over an increased risk of hacking attacks.

Felix Kuhlenkamp, head of security at German digital industry association Bitkom, said that many larger operators had already carried out updates, but that for complex IT systems and smaller organizations it could take longer.

"They may run a website using PHP but don't really keep a close eye on it," he said. "If a website is based on an old version of PHP for which there is no security update, the entire system must be updated."

England captain Harry Brook smashed the fastest double ton in One-Day International history and became the first Englishman to score 200 in the format as he powered his side to 429-4 against Sri Lanka in their tri-series match in Rawalpindi on Thursday.

The 27-year-old rewrote the record books by racing to his double hundred in 114 balls, surpassing the previous mark of 117 deliveries set by India's Shubman Gill.

In the process, Brook also eclipsed England's highest individual ODI score of 182, held by all-rounder Ben Stokes.

Brook's scintillating performance ended with the final ball of England's innings when he was caught by Sahan Arachchige off the bowling of Janith Liyanage.

He made 202 from 116 deliveries, peppering the Sri Lanka attack with 21 fours and 10 sixes before departing to warm applause from the crowd.

Joe Root provided strong support with 69 from 66 balls, finishing as England's second-highest scorer of the day.

item.title: New colours, old buses as Dhaka prepares another transport overhaul
item.description:
Dhaka’s latest attempt to bring order to its chaotic bus network will begin on November 1, but passengers are unlikely to see many new vehicles.
Most of the buses will be the same ones already operating on the city’s roads, repaired and repainted under a new company-based system.
The government plans to introduce the service on six routes with a proposed fleet of 816 buses, bringing competing operators together under designated companies.
The aim is to stop the race for passengers, introduce disciplined boarding and ticketing, and gradually replace the city’s fragmented bus network.
But with electronic ticketing arrangements still unsettled, many designated stops missing and bus owners reluctant to abandon existing practices, the initiative faces obstacles similar to those that derailed earlier reforms.
The Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority (DTCA) says replacing thousands of buses immediately is not feasible. Instead, owners have been given two months to repair and repaint existing vehicles, while those found unfit are to be excluded.
That could leave the initial fleet smaller than planned.
Dhrubo Alam, deputy transport planner at the DTCA, told Dhaka Tribune that previous attempts failed partly because the authorities had imposed decisions without sufficiently involving bus owners.
“Whenever an initiative was taken, the government made decisions without coordinating with the owners’ associations. It simply imposed its decisions,” he said.
This time, the authorities intend to work with operators while conducting joint drives against unauthorised buses and vehicles without valid fitness certificates or route permits.
The initial rollout will cover five non-air-conditioned routes and one air-conditioned route, connecting Gazipur, Mirpur, Keraniganj, Ghatarchar, Demra, Kanchpur and other major destinations.
The air-conditioned service will run from Tongi Airport through the expressway and Farmgate to Azimpur and Dhakeshwari Temple.
The plan follows an October 8 meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, where the authorities were directed to accelerate bus route rationalisation.
Dhaka currently has around 7,500 buses operated by 66 companies on just 98 of its 418 approved routes, according to the DTCA.
Under the proposed overhaul, the 98 operating routes will eventually be consolidated into 32, with one designated company responsible for each route.
Officials say around 70% of the proposed routes will follow existing alignments, although some passengers may need to change buses to reach their destinations.
The government wants franchise arrangements for all 32 routes finalised within two months and the overall program completed within six months.
One of the biggest unresolved issues is how passengers will pay fares.
The new system is supposed to introduce electronic and counter-based ticketing, GPS tracking and designated boarding points.
But DTCA sources said bus owners on all but one of the 32 proposed routes have yet to agree to electronic ticketing.
An official acknowledged that even setting up ticket counters had proved difficult, raising doubts about how quickly a digital system could be introduced.
The experience of previous initiatives offers little reassurance.
A 2024 DTCA inspection found that 165 of approximately 400 designated bus stops across eight pilot routes had not been implemented.
Without functioning ticketing systems, passengers eventually returned to paying fares directly after boarding.
The authorities are also considering monthly salaries for drivers and helpers to replace commission-based earnings, widely blamed for aggressive competition between buses.
Kadir Molla, a bus driver on the Sadarghat route, said the proposed single-operator arrangement could reduce that competition.
“If only one company’s buses operate on this route, we will no longer have to compete with other buses for passengers,” he said.
Bus route rationalisation has been discussed in Dhaka for more than two decades.
The proposal appeared in the 2004 Strategic Transport Plan and was revived by former Dhaka North mayor Annisul Huq in 2015.
A pilot service between Ghatarchar and Kanchpur began in December 2021 but failed to expand as planned amid resistance from operators.
Another attempt on the Gabtoli–Chashara route in 2025 also fell short.
More recently, the BRTC’s Pink Bus service for women, launched in August with repainted buses, encountered operational difficulties within two months.
Passenger welfare advocates fear the new initiative could meet the same fate.
Mozammel Haque Chowdhury, secretary general of the Bangladesh Passenger Welfare Association, questioned whether reorganising operators and repainting existing buses would substantially improve services.
He said the government should have introduced new vehicles and consulted passenger representatives during planning.
Urban planner Adil Mohammad Khan said the initiative could succeed only if unauthorised buses were prevented from competing with the designated operators.
“Stopping parallel bus services opens up a new possibility,” he said.
However, he stressed that vehicle quality could not be ignored, particularly given Dhaka’s heat and heavy passenger demand.
He called for a clear deadline to introduce modern, air-conditioned buses at affordable fares, alongside functioning stops and ticketing systems.
The DTCA separately plans to introduce new, smaller buses on 25 circular routes connecting to the metro rail network in about two months.
For the November 1 rollout, however, commuters will largely be boarding familiar vehicles. Whether they receive a different service will depend on changes that have repeatedly proved harder to deliver than new paint.

item.title: Eight years after safe roads movement, deaths keep mounting
item.description:
Eight years after the deaths of two students sparked a nationwide movement for safer roads, Bangladesh is still struggling to curb the carnage, with more than 9,000 people killed in road crashes last year alone, according to a transport rights organisation.
The slogans of the 2018 movement may still be visible on walls, but the figures tell a grim story of how little progress has been made in preventing deaths on the country’s roads.
According to Bangladesh Jatri Kalyan Samity, at least 95,761 people were killed and 168,000 injured in 69,448 road crashes between 2014 and 2025.
The organisation recorded 9,111 deaths in 2025, compared with 7,221 in 2018, an increase of about 26%.
The Road Safety Foundation (RSF), which uses a different method of compiling crash data, recorded 7,359 deaths in 2025.
Although the estimates differ, both point to a heavy toll that continues despite years of demands for reform.
The 2018 movement, triggered by the deaths of two students in Dhaka, brought thousands of young people onto the streets.
Their demands went beyond punishment for reckless drivers: they wanted a transport system in which vehicles were fit to operate, drivers were properly trained and traffic laws were enforced.
Eight years later, many of those problems remain.
RSF Executive Director Saidur Rahman identified excessive speed, unfit vehicles, poor road design, inadequate driver training and weak enforcement as major causes of crashes.
But he said the problem extends beyond what happens behind the wheel.
Many bus and truck drivers work without appointment letters, fixed salaries or regulated working hours. The resulting pressure and fatigue can contribute to dangerous driving, he said.
“Most accidents occur because drivers lose control of their vehicles due to excessive speed,” Saidur told Bangla Tribune.
He called for technology-based speed monitoring, better driver training and stronger oversight of the transport sector.
He also urged reforms to the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA), saying the regulatory system needed greater transparency and accountability.
Bangladesh Jatri Kalyan Samity Secretary General Mozammel Haque Chowdhury called for modernising vehicle fitness checks, removing vehicles that have exceeded their operational lifespan and introducing technology-based traffic enforcement.
The recommendations are hardly new.
Road safety organisations have repeatedly called for better highways, trained drivers, effective enforcement and action against extortion in public transport.

item.title: Biman suspends Riyadh, Dammam flights over security concerns
item.description:
Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended flights from Dhaka to Dammam on Friday, Saturday and Sunday, and all Dhaka-Riyadh flights until October 31, citing passenger safety amid the ongoing security situation in Saudi Arabia.
The airline’s public relations department confirmed the decisions on Thursday night.
Further decisions on the suspended flights and revised schedules will be announced in due course, the department said.
Flights from Dhaka to Jeddah and Medina will continue to operate according to their existing schedules.
Passengers travelling to Dammam and Riyadh may use Jeddah and Medina international airports to travel to Saudi Arabia or return to Bangladesh, subject to seat availability, the department said.
Passengers have been advised to contact their nearest Biman Bangladesh Airlines sales centre for ticketing and travel-related information.

item.title: New registration, old fears for Dhaka’s street vendors
item.description:
Dhaka’s street food vendors are preparing to enter a formal registration system from November 1, hoping it will give their businesses legal recognition and protection from harassment.
But many fear that a government certificate will do little to stop the extortion and eviction threats they face on the streets.
“If local leaders still demand money after we get licences, those licences will have no value,” said Mohammad Helal, 21, who sells fruit juice in Gulistan.
His concern reflects the uncertainty surrounding the Bangladesh Safe Food Authority’s (BFSA) decision to bring street food sellers and other small food businesses under a mandatory registration system.
Under the Safe Food (Registration and Licence) Regulations, 2026, issued on July 16, registration will be required for 16 categories of food businesses, including vendors selling pitha, puri, piyaju, jhalmuri and fruit juice.
The BFSA will begin accepting applications on November 1, with first-time registration free of charge.
For many vendors, the move offers the prospect of greater recognition in a sector where livelihoods often depend on informal arrangements.
Mohammad Abul Hasan, 30, who sells jhalmuri and piyaju, said he hoped registration would help protect traders from arbitrary eviction and illegal payments.
“If we follow whatever the government decides, our business will become legitimate. That will end the fear of eviction, and the practice of illegal extortion may also stop,” he said.
Zahirul Islam, a 24-year-old puri seller in Panthapath, also welcomed the decision, saying traders should comply with government regulations.
But whether registration will provide any protection against eviction or extortion remains unclear.
Street vendors say the authorities must address the conditions under which they operate, rather than simply issue registration documents.
Jahangir Mia, a fruit seller at Karwan Bazar, said roadside food businesses provide affordable options for ordinary consumers.
“Food that costs Tk40 on the street may cost Tk60 to Tk80 in a market,” he said, adding that designated spaces should be provided so vendors can operate without obstructing pedestrians.
Another hawker, speaking anonymously, questioned whether the authorities could enforce registration limits.
He cited an instance in which only 20 licences had been issued but around 2,000 hawkers were operating in the area.
“Without strict control, issuing licences will achieve nothing,” he said.
The concerns go beyond extortion. Vendors also want clarity about the documents required, future renewal fees and possible penalties for non-compliance.
BFSA Chairman Md Safiqul Islam said registration would help the authority identify food businesses, bring greater discipline to their operations and arrange training where necessary.
He said monitoring was essential to prevent public health risks associated with unsafe food preparation and handling.
The chairman assured traders that they would not be harassed under the new system.
The registration requirement extends beyond street vendors to restaurants, bakeries, sweet shops, caterers, packaged food producers, dairy businesses, grocery wholesalers and food warehouses.
Certain specialised businesses will also need paid licences in addition to registration.
However, Bangladesh Restaurant Owners Association Secretary General Imran Hasan criticised the introduction of another regulatory process alongside existing licensing requirements.
He warned that overlapping rules could expose traders to additional harassment and fines.
Imran said the authorities should have consulted stakeholders and developed an integrated system instead.
For small vendors, the immediate concern is more practical: whether they can complete the registration process without complicated paperwork or additional expenses.
Food safety advocates and other observers have called for simplified applications, clear instructions and hygiene training for traders.

item.title: PM inspects Mongla Port, Sundarbans, proposed economic zone
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday inspected Mongla Port, the Sundarbans and the site of a proposed economic zone in Bagerhat during a daylong visit to the southwestern region, raising hopes among local residents and businesspeople for fresh investment, infrastructure development and economic growth there.
He left Dhaka by helicopter around 9am and flew over parts of the Sundarbans, including Hiron Point, to observe the world's largest mangrove forest after reaching the southwestern part.
The helicopter later landed at the Nalian Secondary School ground in Dakop upazila of Khulna around 10:30am.
The prime minister then travelled by waterway to BNS Mongla, a Bangladesh Navy facility in Bagerhat, where he met Navy officials, port authorities and local administration officials at the wardroom.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit, State Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shaikh Faridul Islam, Whip Rakibul Islam, Khulna Divisional Commissioner Md Abdulla Harun, Mongla Port Authority Chairman Rear Admiral Arif Ahmed Mostafa, Bagerhat Deputy Commissioner Golam Md Baten, Superintendent of Police Md Jamirul Islam, and senior officials of the Navy and Coast Guard were present.
After the meeting and lunch, Tarique Rahman inspected the jetty facilities and operations of Mongla Port.
He later visited the site of the proposed economic zone planned by the Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority (BEZA).
The prime minister left Mongla for Dhaka by helicopter around 5pm after completing his engagements.
Security was tightened across the Sundarbans, Dakop and Mongla areas during the prime minister's visit, with members of law enforcement and security agencies deployed to ensure the smooth conduct of his engagements.
During the visit, local residents gathered to greet the prime minister and expressed their hopes for development in the region.
They expected the visit to bring renewed government attention to the area's long-standing development needs.
Local businesspeople also expressed hope that the prime minister's visit will help address long-standing problems facing Mongla Port and the surrounding industrial areas.
Businessman Firoz Ahmed said the prime minister’s visit raised hopes for development and will help improve the livelihoods of people in the region.
Another businessman, Hemayet Uddin, said the southwestern region, including Mongla, had long been neglected.
He said infrastructure development is essential for business growth and economic progress, expressing hope that the prime minister’s visit will help accelerate development in the area.
Hamayet also said the proposed economic zone will create jobs for a large number of people in Mongla, while the launch of an LNG terminal will facilitate the expansion of trade and commerce across the region.
BNP leader Hafizur Rahman Tuhin said the port's development, the proposed LNG terminal near Akram Point and the economic zone will significantly boost the regional economy.
He also stressed the need to resolve problems related to jetty facilities and dredging.
Md Julfikar Ali, general secretary of the Mongla Port Berth and Ship Operators’ Association, said the development of floating storage regasification unit (FSRU) facilities will help meet the region's energy needs and support industrial growth.
Sheikh Sahed Ali Robi, president of the Bagerhat Chamber of Commerce and Industry, stressed the need for regular dredging to maintain the navigability of the port channel and modernise customs services to make port operations more efficient.
State Minister Faridul said industrialisation and investment centred on Mongla Port will create jobs and improve livelihoods in the coastal region, including for people affected by climate change.
He said coordinated development of the port, the proposed economic zone and tourism in the Sundarbans will help transform the southwestern region into a major centre for trade and investment.

item.title: Rangamati, Khagrachhari roads and waterways to face half-day blockade
item.description:
Roads and waterways in Rangamati and Khagrachhari districts will be blockaded for 7 hours on Saturday following a call by the Chhatra-Janatar Sangram Parishad to protest attacks on blockade participants, baton charges and vandalism of homes and shops in Sajek, Baghai Chhari upazila of Rangamati.
The program was announced by the organization’s president, Ushaton Chakma, in a statement sent to the media on Thursday afternoon.
The statement said the blockade was called in protest against attacks, baton charges and vandalism during a peaceful road blockade demanding the removal of armed members of the JSS Santu Group from Sajek. It was also announced in support of Sajek residents’ demands.
According to the announcement, the blockade will remain in force across the 2 districts from 5am to 12 noon on Saturday.
Ushaton Chakma sought cooperation from democratic and progressive organizations in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, as well as transport owners’ and workers’ organizations in Rangamati and Khagrachhari, to make the program successful.
Ambulances and vehicles carrying patients, dead bodies or emergency medicines, as well as fire service vehicles and vehicles carrying journalists, will remain exempt from the blockade.

item.title: BB website taken offline amid global cyber threat
item.description:
The website of Bangladesh Bank on Thursday was temporarily shut down to avoid the risk of a cyber attack.
The website could not be accessed as Bangladesh Bank stated that this step was taken to review security risks and ensure necessary safeguard measures.
Upon accessing the central bank's main website (bb.org.bd), a message reading: "The Service is under Maintenance" is displayed. Below it, it further states: "Our service is currently undergoing scheduled maintenance. We will be back online shortly. Thank you for your patience. Bangladesh Bank."
In other words, the service has been temporarily suspended for scheduled maintenance work and will be back online soon.
Arief Hossain Khan, executive director and spokesperson of Bangladesh Bank, told reporters: "Bangladesh Bank's website has been kept offline to avoid the risk of a global cyber attack. This step was taken as a precautionary measure to prevent security risks."
He added: "Bangladesh Bank's IT department is working to identify and resolve security vulnerabilities on the website. We hope to make the website operational again very soon."
According to a report by AFP, two critical security vulnerabilities were recently identified in PHP, a widely used programming language for website development and management.
According to cybersecurity firm Wiz, attackers could exploit these flaws to remotely execute unauthorized commands on servers. This could put server files, databases, and sensitive information at risk.
In light of this situation, government institutions in several countries, including France, the Netherlands, and Belgium, have proactively shut down their websites as a precaution.
However, identifying a security flaw does not necessarily mean a website has been attacked.
It is reported that PHP is a widely used server-side programming language.
This technology is used to run government and private institutions, news media, e-commerce platforms, and various online services. Many websites in Bangladesh are also PHP-based.

item.title: Bangladesh, Algeria seek broader cooperation in energy, agriculture, textiles
item.description:
Bangladesh and Algeria discussed expanding bilateral cooperation in energy, trade, agriculture, fertilisers, textiles, education, and other sectors on Thursday for the mutual benefit of both countries.
The discussions took place at a bilateral meeting between State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir and Algerian Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf in Algiers, where the two sides also shed light on regional and multilateral issues of mutual concern.
They discussed ways to expand bilateral trade and investment, particularly in the energy sector.
Referring to the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed between Bangladesh and Algeria recently on hydrocarbon cooperation, Kobir said the engagement has opened a new horizon for Bangladesh to import liquefied natural gas (LNG), liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and other petroleum products from the North African country under a government-to-government (G2G) arrangement.
The MoU also offers scope for cooperation in refinery development, LNG infrastructure and the exploration of coal and gas fields in Bangladesh, he said.
The Algerian Petroleum Institute expressed interest in providing a training and knowledge-sharing program for Bangladeshi engineers and technicians in the field of energy, developing self-reliance energy skills in Bangladesh.
Attaf said the Algerian president had directed that the hydrocarbon MoU be signed on a priority basis in response to Bangladesh's energy needs.
On fertilizer cooperation, he expressed Algeria's willingness to work with Bangladesh to help meet the country's fertilizer requirements and support its agricultural sector.
The minister also sought Bangladesh's experience in reviving Algeria's textile industry and expressed interest in cooperation in the pharmaceutical, leather and textile sectors.
Both sides underscored the importance of holding Foreign Office Consultations regularly, and the next round of consultations will be held in Dhaka soon.
The two sides discussed the importance of exchanging high-level visits to further consolidate the existing bilateral relations between the two countries.

item.title: Guitarist Russell Khan dies at 52
item.description:
Guitarist Russell Khan, who accompanied many of Bangladesh’s leading singers for more than three decades, died at his elder sister’s home in Dhaka’s Banani on Thursday. He was 52.
Instrumentalist Azmir Babu confirmed his death to the media.
Russell had been unwell for several days after contracting dengue and chikungunya. He reportedly collapsed in the bathroom at his sister’s home on Thursday morning. A doctor later examined him and pronounced him dead, with a stroke cited as the cause of death.
Over a career spanning more than three decades, Russell performed alongside many of the country’s prominent singers, becoming a familiar face on stage. Besides playing the guitar, he occasionally performed as a vocalist.
His last stage performance was at an event in Manikganj on October 13.
Following news of his death, fellow musicians, artistes, and well-wishers took to Facebook to share condolences and memories of working with him.
His namaz-e-janaza was held at 3:30pm on Thursday at a mosque near his sister’s home in Banani. His body was then being taken to his ancestral home in Bikrampur for burial at the family graveyard.
He is survived by his wife, a son, and a daughter.

item.title: Moyeen Khan’s condition stable, says Zahid
item.description:
Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan, who was hospitalized on Wednesday night with breathing and heart-related problems, is now in stable condition, said BNP Standing Committee Member Prof Dr AZM Zahid Hossain on Thursday.
He shared the information after visiting Moyeen Khan, also a BNP Standing Committee member, at Evercare Hospital Dhaka in the afternoon.
“He was admitted to the hospital on Wednesday after falling ill with breathing and heart-related problems. He is receiving treatment under close observation by the doctors,” Zahid said, adding that his condition is now more stable than it was on Wednesday.
Zahid, also the social welfare, women and children affairs minister, said Moyeen Khan is undergoing treatment under the supervision of Evercare Hospital physicians Dr Kazi Atiqur Rahman, Dr Ziaul Huq and Dr Zafor Iqbal.
In the evening, BNP acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi also visited Moyeen Khan at the hospital.
During the visit, the doctors briefed him on his latest condition.
Earlier, Moyeen Khan was taken to Evercare Hospital on Wednesday night after he fell ill.
The family has urged the country’s people to pray for his speedy recovery.

item.title: Rang Bilash sugarcane emerges as profitable crop in Natore
item.description:
With its distinctive colour, juicy stalks and growing demand as a chewing sugarcane, Rang Bilash is emerging as a promising cash crop in Natore, creating new income opportunities for farmers in the Chalan Beel region.
Farmers in three upazilas of the district are increasingly cultivating the variety, encouraged by its good yield and lucrative returns. This year, Rang Bilash has been cultivated on 126 hectares of land in Natore, with an estimated production of 1,213 tonnes of sugarcane juice.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), Gurudaspur has the largest area under cultivation, with 60 hectares, followed by Baraigram with 52 hectares and Singra with 14 hectares.
Cultivation of the variety is concentrated in these three upazilas bordering the Chalan Beel region, where favourable soil, water availability and climatic conditions support its growth.
Farmers said the crop's profitability stems not only from sugarcane sales but also from the opportunity to grow lucrative intercrops between the rows of cane.
Rabiul Karim, a farmer, told Dhaka Tribune that he grows garlic or onion between the sugarcane rows after planting the seedlings.
“We get around 25 to 30 maunds of garlic per bigha. In the case of onion, the yield can reach as high as 60 maunds,” he said.
According to Rabiul, earnings from intercrops can cover almost the entire cost of sugarcane cultivation, allowing farmers to earn substantial profits from selling the cane.
“With intercropping, a farmer can earn at least Tk2 lakh in profit per bigha,” he said.
For Golam Rasul of Mahishbhanga village in Baraigram, ‘RangBilash’ is more than a seasonal crop. He has been cultivating the variety for nearly three decades.
Rasul has already prepared more than 1,000 seedlings in his nursery for the next season. He said the crop remains in the field throughout the year and requires regular care.
“The plants need proper care, particularly protection from fungal attacks. If that is ensured, the yield is very good,” he told Dhaka Tribune.
This year, Rasul cultivated ‘RangBilash’ on five bighas of land and has already sold sugarcane harvested from two bighas for Tk4.5 lakh.
Traders from outside Natore are visiting his fields to buy the cane directly. He sells 100 stalks for Tk3,000 to Tk7,000, while retail prices range from Tk40 to Tk80 per stalk, depending on size and quality.
Selim Reza, sub-assistant agriculture officer of the Bonpara agricultural block, said farmers were also growing mung beans alongside garlic and onion in sugarcane fields.
“Intercropping makes ‘RangBilash’ cultivation highly profitable. Farmers can benefit considerably by adopting this method,” he said.
Around 100 acres of land in his agricultural block have been brought under ‘RangBilash’ cultivation this season, he added.
Baraigram Upazila Agriculture Officer Nilima Jahan said cultivation of the variety was helping improve farmers’ financial conditions in the area.
“The agriculture department is providing farmers with the necessary advice and technical support to expand cultivation of the variety,” she said.
Gurudaspur Upazila Agriculture Officer AKM Rafiul Islam said the upazila currently leads the district in ‘RangBilash’ cultivation.
“Many enthusiastic farmers in the upazila have taken up sugarcane cultivation because of its profitability,” he said.
DAE Deputy Director Md Habibul Islam Khan said farmers in the Chalan Beel region were already benefiting from the cultivation of ‘RangBilash’.
“Chewing sugarcane of this variety is gradually becoming an important cash crop for farmers in the Chalan Beel region. It has the potential to emerge as one of the area's major commercial crops in the near future,” he told Dhaka Tribune.
With strong market demand and the added advantage of profitable intercropping, Rang Bilash is opening up new income opportunities for Natore farmers, potentially establishing itself as a major commercial crop in the Chalan Beel region.

item.title: Action plans by Sunday to prepare for April-March FY
item.description:
The Ministry of Housing and Public Works has sought time-bound action plans from its subordinate offices and agencies to implement the decision to introduce an April-March fiscal year (FY), replacing the existing July-June fiscal year.
To this end, the ministry has directed the concerned offices and agencies to review relevant laws, rules, circulars, statutory regulatory orders (SRO), contracts and memorandums of understanding (MoU) and submit plans for necessary amendments and coordination by Sunday.
The directive was issued in a letter by Administration Branch-6 of the ministry on October 15. Signed by Deputy Secretary Mohammad Abdul Awal, the letter was sent to various departments, authorities and relevant branches under the ministry, including the Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (Rajuk).
According to the letter, the government has decided to replace the long-standing July-June fiscal year with an April-March fiscal year. At a cabinet meeting held on August 17, it was decided to treat the 2027-28 fiscal year as a transitional fiscal year, with its duration shortened from 12 months to nine months, covering July to March of the following year.
Subsequently, the government planned to introduce the period from April 1 to March 31 as fiscal year from 2028-29, with government activities to be conducted accordingly.
The letter stated that the necessary legal framework for implementing the new fiscal year structure must be established before the start of the 2027-28 fiscal year, meaning the work must be completed within the current fiscal year.
It also said the change in the fiscal year would require necessary modifications and adjustments to the government's Annual Development Programme (ADP), overall development activities, national production and statistical frameworks and information technology and software-based systems.
Relevant government systems, including iBAS++, VAT and treasury management, would also need to be aligned with the new fiscal year.
The ministry further instructed that relevant laws, rules, circulars, SRO, contracts, MoU, and statistical and information technology frameworks under each ministry and division be reviewed thoroughly.
Based on the review, specific and time-bound action plans must be formulated by identifying areas requiring amendments, additions, revisions and coordination.
The initiative is expected to strengthen the legal and institutional foundations for government operations under the new fiscal year system if the required measures are implemented within the stipulated timeframe.
The directive has been sent to Rajuk, the Department of Urban Development, the National Housing Authority, the Public Works Department, the Department of Architecture, the Directorate of Government Accommodation and the Housing and Building Research Institute.
Development authorities in Chittagong, Rajshahi, Khulna, Sylhet, Barisal, Mymensingh, Gazipur, Narayanganj, Comilla, Rangpur and Cox's Bazar, along with other relevant offices and agencies, have also been brought under the directive.
Various branches of the ministry, including administration, law, planning and development, audit, land management, abandoned property management and ICT, have also been involved in the process.
The letter stated that all concerned offices and agencies must review matters under their respective jurisdictions and take necessary steps to implement the decision to change the fiscal year.

item.title: Interns suspend work stoppage at RMCH
item.description:
Intern doctors at Rajshahi Medical College Hospital (RMCH) have suspended their work stoppage and said they will resume duties this (Friday) morning.
The decision was made on Thursday following a meeting with hospital director Brig Gen PKM Masud-ul-Islam, said hospital spokesperson Dr Sheikh Shamim Ahmed.
“The interns held lengthy discussions with the hospital director over their demands. They have since suspended the work stoppage and will return to work on Friday morning,” he said.
Around 250 intern doctors began the work stoppage on Wednesday morning to press home their five-point demand, causing suffering for patients seeking treatment at the hospital.
Their demands include ensuring adequate supplies of medicines and medical equipment in inpatient wards, guaranteeing the safety of intern doctors, restricting the number of patient attendants entering the hospital to two per patient, ensuring the active presence of Ansar members in all wards on the day of admission and the following day, and immediately launching the casualty department.

item.title: Andaleeve: Awami League’s no democracy narrative won’t gain ground
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Barrister Andaleeve Rahman on Thursday said the Awami League is trying to build a new narrative abroad that there is no democracy in Bangladesh, stressing that there is no scope for such a narrative to gain ground in the country.
“Democracy is a process. It is taking time to recover from the system destroyed over the past 17 years. People have voted us, we have been elected, and we have an opposition. I believe democracy will improve further and reach a better position,” he said.
The minister made the remarks while responding to questions from journalists during a visit to Bankerhat Bazar in Bhola Sadar upazila in the evening.
Andaleeve, also chairman of Bangladesh Jatiya Party (BJP), exchanged greetings with party leaders and activists.
He said the Awami League had previously claimed that Hindu religious festivals would not be held in the country if the BNP came to power. “However, Hindus celebrated their religious festivals this year peacefully and amid festivities.”
The minister said he had never before witnessed such a beautiful and secure celebration of Durga Puja in Bangladesh as he saw this year.
He said shortly after the Awami League was ousted, a campaign began claiming that Hindus were being persecuted in Bangladesh, alleging that some Indian media outlets were also trying to spread such claims.
Andaleeve said nearly 5 crore people aged between 15 and 35 were directly or indirectly involved in the fall of the Awami League.
Given the involvement of such a large number of people, it will be very difficult for the Awami League to regain public support through its narrative, he added.

item.title: French authorities seek to ban or curb fresh protests
item.description:
French authorities on Thursday imposed bans or restrictions on fresh protests springing up in the wake of demonstrations last weekend that degenerated into the worst street violence in years.
President Emmanuel Macron said, after chairing a meeting of key ministers and intelligence officials, that curfews and other security measures would be imposed, including bans on “groups without legitimacy” holding protests.
“The priority is a return to calm,” he said, adding that he would chair a defense council meeting of key ministers on Friday to decide “the next steps” for new nationwide demonstrations called for Saturday and afterwards.
Officials are still reeling from the clashes, widespread looting and vandalism of public buildings that broke out on October 17, on the margins of mass demonstrations of more than half a million people against the surging cost of living.
Macron’s government has admitted police lost control, and candidates jockeying to succeed him in presidential elections in six months’ time argue that authorities are incapable or unwilling to calm the situation.
The worst of the violence, Macron said, “was led by organized ultra-left groups aiming to bring down the republic.”
A Paris protest Thursday organized by students -- who had held four weeks of protests before the October 17 rallies -- was banned by the capital’s police.
“The authorities are trying to make a distinction between ‘good’ and ‘bad’ protesters,” said a university student leader, Coppelia Moreau, as lawyers requested a court injunction against the ban.
“What we are seeing is a government that doesn’t want any demonstrations at all. That goes against the right to demonstrate,” she told journalists.
Authorities on Thursday also declared a ban on “all protests” in the southwestern city of Lyon on Saturday.
France’s third-biggest city suffered the looting of 200 to 300 shops last weekend and the torching of a tourist office in what its mayor described as hours of “chaos.”
Other cities, including Grenoble, Rouen, Le Havre and Toulon, issued bans on protests in their city centers.
In Paris, the city’s police said Thursday that the march planned for Saturday could be held in the east of the capital, starting at Bastille, but was banned from heading into the city center, where shops and major public buildings are located.
The Yellow Vest movement organizing the cost-of-living rallies along with unions said it did not agree with the order.
“We won’t sign off on it,” said Benjamin Ball, who runs an online map showing the planned locations of Saturday’s demonstrations.
The French government has been projecting a firm response in the wake of last weekend’s violence, although Macron has said he would not go as far as to call a state of emergency.
Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said Wednesday that 174 people of the 2,500 arrested since last weekend had been locked up, and more than 900 were being prosecuted.
On Thursday, a 66-year-old man was arrested over the arson last weekend of the 19th-century town hall of Limoges, prosecutors said. A man in his 30s was already arrested Tuesday over the same crime.
Marine Le Pen, the far-right leader whom voter surveys place as the frontrunner candidate ahead of the April-May presidential elections, has accused Macron and his centrist government of being too soft and lacking authority.
Jean-Luc Melenchon, a far-left candidate criticized by the government for not condemning the protest violence, blamed authorities’ “non-stop brutal repression” for the unrest.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Thursday was to host a meeting of top officials from France’s main parties to hear their grievances and seek cooperation. While most were sending their leaders, Le Pen’s National Rally was to be represented by a lower-ranking party official.
Lecornu was to follow that up with another meeting with mayors, and on Monday he will meet student groups.

item.title: James Bond auction features Craig’s ‘Skyfall’ Suit, de Armas’ Dress
item.description:
Daniel Craig’s suit from “Skyfall” and Ana de Armas’ dress from “No Time to Die” are among more than 400 lots featured in an online auction of James Bond memorabilia organised by Propstore.
Running from October 6 to 27, the auction features costumes, props, posters and literary collectibles from the long-running film franchise, spanning 6 decades of James Bond’s screen history.
Craig’s grey Tom Ford suit, worn in the 2012 film “Skyfall”, is among the sale’s most valuable items, with an estimated price of £20,000–£40,000, equivalent to approximately Tk 3.3 million–Tk 6.6 million.
The suit appeared in the film’s opening sequence in Istanbul, where Bond pursues an assassin across rooftops and onto a moving train. The lot also includes the accompanying shirt, tie and cufflinks.
A navy dress and sandals worn by de Armas as CIA agent Paloma in “No Time to Die” (2021) carry the same estimate. The outfit appears in the film’s Cuba sequence, where Paloma joins Bond on an operation.
The auction also features a British quad poster for “Dr. No” (1962), the first James Bond film, with an estimated price of £8,000–£16,000, or approximately Tk 1.3 million–Tk 2.65 million. The film introduced Sean Connery as the British secret agent and launched the screen franchise.
Literary collectibles include a complete set of 14 first editions and first impressions of Ian Fleming’s James Bond books, published by Jonathan Cape. Estimated at £20,000–£40,000, the collection comprises 12 novels and two short-story collections, rebound in leather and housed in a matching slipcase.
Another lot is a hardback first edition of Fleming’s 1958 novel “Dr. No”, in its third impression, signed by Connery, Bernard Lee and Joseph Wiseman. Connery played Bond in the film adaptation, Lee portrayed M, the head of the British Secret Service, and Wiseman played the title character.
The sale brings together production memorabilia from across the franchise, alongside books and printed material connected to Fleming’s original stories.
The online auction closes on October 27. Bidders can view the catalogue and participate through Propstore’s website.

item.title: ‘Ice Cream’ returns to screens on OTT a decade after theatrical release
item.description:
A decade after its theatrical release, Redoan Rony’s Ice Cream, which marked the film debuts of Sariful Razz, Nazifa Tushi and Kumar Uday, is set to arrive on streaming platform Chorki at midnight on October 20.
Written and directed by Rony, the film was released in cinemas on April 29, 2016, and marked an important milestone in the careers of its three debutant actors.
Looking back on her first film, Tushi recalled entering the industry with little knowledge of filmmaking but a strong desire to act.
“I stepped into cinema without knowing or understanding how vast a canvas it was. I knew nothing about the industry. All I knew was that I wanted to act,” she said.
Tushi said the film stood out to her at a time when relatively few alternative films were being made outside the Film Development Corporation (FDC).
“I felt ‘Ice Cream’ was a good film and Redoan Rony was a good director. I was young, and that was enough for me to think I could do it,” she said.
The experience, she added, taught her much about filmmaking and the industry. Reflecting on the passage of time, she said it was surprising to realise that a decade had passed since she made her debut.
For Razz, the film remains a defining chapter in his professional journey. He said the actor he was a decade ago differs from the person he has become, but Ice Cream helped lay the foundation for his career.
“The rehearsals, the nervousness behind the camera, Redoan Rony bhai’s guidance and the moments on set are still vivid,” he said.
Razz added that the film’s arrival on Chorki would give audiences an opportunity to revisit his early days as an actor and see the enthusiasm with which he first stepped in front of the camera.
“It feels truly surreal,” he said.
At the time of the film’s theatrical release, Razz had also spoken emotionally about the struggles that led him to his first film, expressing gratitude to Rony for the opportunity.
Explaining the film’s title, Rony, who wrote its story, screenplay and dialogue, previously compared a relationship to ice cream, saying it needed to be maintained at a particular temperature.
The film’s soundtrack features vocals by Arnob, Armeen Musa, Sharmin Sultana Sumi and Minar Rahman.
The cast also includes ATM Shamsuzzaman, Diti, Omar Sani, Sayem Sadat and Nadia Khanam.
With its arrival on Chorki, Ice Cream offers viewers a chance to revisit a film that marked the beginning of three acting careers and remains a significant milestone in the journeys of its lead performers.

item.title: Liberation DocFest selects 17 documentaries from 188 submissions
item.description:
The 13th edition of Liberation DocFest Bangladesh will showcase 17 documentaries selected from 188 submissions at the Liberation War Museum in Agargaon, Dhaka, from October 29 to 31.
This year’s festival, themed “Presence in Absence”, will feature national and international competition sections alongside a “Best of the Fest” programme.
An eight-member preview committee selected the films from submissions by filmmakers across different countries. The committee comprised Jihan Karim, Biplob Sarkar, Mehedi Mostafa, Partha Sarathi, Sharmin Doza, Chaitali Samaddar, Kamrul Ahsan and Kazi Arefin Ahmed.
The selected documentaries are organised into eight thematic sections: “Bodies and Belonging”, “Gender Equality and Resistance”, “Resistance and Reform”, “Generational Memory”, “Displacement and Statelessness”, “1971: Living Archives”, “Ecology in Crisis” and “Ancestral Roots and Livelihoods”.
The national and international competition winners will each receive prize money of Tk 1 lakh. A separate nine-member youth jury will also select a film for recognition, with the winner receiving a crest and certificate.
The national jury comprises filmmaker Shabnam Ferdousi, visual artist and filmmaker Dilara Begum, and Sajjad Hossain, a faculty member at the University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh.
The international jury includes cultural personality M Hamid, filmmaker Shamim Akhtar and human rights activist Asif Munier.
Alongside the screenings, the festival will host a seminar on documentary filmmaking in higher education. The discussion will explore the opportunities and practical challenges of incorporating documentary production into classroom projects, with particular attention to how the medium can connect younger generations with the history and memory of the Liberation War.
The seminar is scheduled for 4pm on October 30 in the museum’s seminar room.
Established in 2006, Liberation DocFest Bangladesh promotes documentary filmmaking focused on freedom, human rights and social struggles. The festival also aims to strengthen connections between Bangladeshi filmmakers and the international documentary film community while encouraging younger generations to engage with the medium.

item.title: Tom Cruise to receive AFI’s highest honour for lifetime achievement
item.description:
Hollywood star Tom Cruise will receive the American Film Institute’s (AFI) 52nd Life Achievement Award, recognising his decades-long contribution to cinema as an actor and producer.
The 64-year-old actor will be honoured at a gala ceremony at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles on April 24, 2027. The event will celebrate his career with tributes from friends and longtime collaborators, highlights from his filmography and an acceptance speech.
Kathleen Kennedy, chair of AFI’s board of trustees, described Cruise as a global icon, praising his dedication to filmmaking and his commitment to the theatrical cinema experience. She also highlighted his belief in cinema’s ability to bring people together, noting his influence on American filmmaking worldwide.
AFI considers the award one of the film industry’s most prestigious career honours.
Across a career spanning 45 years, Cruise has starred in films that have collectively earned nearly $13 billion at the global box office. He has received three Academy Award nominations for acting and another as a producer of Top Gun: Maverick. In 2025, he also received an honorary Oscar.
His extensive filmography includes Risky Business, Rain Man, A Few Good Men, The Firm, Jerry Maguire, Magnolia and Minority Report. He is also widely recognised for leading the blockbuster franchises Mission: Impossible and Top Gun.
Cruise most recently starred in Digger, directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu.
Beyond his Oscar recognition, Cruise has received honours from the Cannes Film Festival and the Producers Guild of America. His other accolades include France’s Knight of the Legion of Honour, the Simon Wiesenthal Center’s Humanitarian Award and the Pioneer Award from the Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Foundation.
AFI is a non-profit organisation dedicated to advancing the moving image as an art form. Proceeds from the award gala will support its arts and education programmes.

item.title: Andaleeve: Works underway to amend laws to ensure equal protection for all
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Barrister Andaleeve Rahman has said the government is working on amending various laws, including the cybersecurity act, to ensure equal protection for all.
"To make this process more effective, discussions are being held with stakeholders, including owners of television channels and newspaper editors,” he said.
The minister said policies are being formulated in such a way that equal protection for media personnel, the administration and commoners is guaranteed, and hoped that this ongoing initiative would soon yield positive results.
He made the remarks while talking to reporters on Wednesday night during a visit to several puja mandaps in his home constituency, Bhola Sadar.
Andaleeve mentioned that members of the Hindu community were celebrating their religious festival this year with great joy and in an atmosphere of harmony.
Regarding the overall security for the puja celebrations, he said, “It is a matter of great satisfaction that everyone -Hindus, Muslims, and all others - is currently getting adequate security.”
He said after speaking with members of the Hindu community and leaders of the puja committees, he learned that there were no security concerns or issues whatsoever during the puja celebrations.
No untoward incidents occurred, and everyone celebrated their religious festival in a joyful atmosphere, he said.
Referring to the killing of a journalist in Netrokona, the information minister said any incident involving a violation of the law - regardless of whether it concerns a journalist or a member of any other profession - will be addressed in accordance with the existing laws.
On Wednesday night, the minister visited puja mandaps at nine temples in Bhola Sadar. During his visit, Andaleeve was accompanied by leaders and activists of Bangladesh Jatiya Party (BJP) and its affiliated organisations.
To ensure a joyful Durga puja celebration, the information minister provided a grant totaling Taka 29 lakh to 29 puja mandaps in Bhola Sadar.
